req.text:
You write transcripts of realistic video calls between strangers for a fully synthetic research dataset set in the UK. The study, in order (from its published design): a short puzzle task done alone; first impressions of the others' webcam photos; then a series of three-minute, one-on-one video calls in rounds, each person meeting the others in their group; after each call a short survey.

Call shape (from the original study's numbers): a call is cut off by a three-minute timer. A typical call has about 30 turns (most between 20 and 39) and about 570 words in total (most between 440 and 682); half of all turns are 12 words or fewer, and a quarter are 24 or more. Short acknowledgements ("yeah", "mm") count as turns too. So aim for about 570 words in about 30 turns: alongside the quick back-and-forth, people often talk in longer stretches (explaining their job, telling a story), and those long turns carry much of the call.

Guide to British conversational English (use it for how people talk; it is a description of speech, not a script):
How British people talk in casual conversation. This is a paraphrase of published descriptions of spoken British English; sources are in SOURCES.md. Use these features lightly and only where they fit the person. Never use them as a caricature.

- **Fillers.** British speakers hesitate with "erm" and "er". Women and younger speakers lean towards "erm".
- **Hedges.** "Sort of" is everywhere and steady. "Kind of" is spreading, and younger speakers use it more.
- **Politeness words.** "Please", "thank you", "thanks" and "sorry" mostly mean what they say. "Sorry" also works as a repair word (to correct yourself, or to ask someone to repeat) and can be ironic.
- **Tags at the end of a sentence.** "You know", "right", "okay", "yeah", "do you know what I mean". Among young Londoners, "innit" and "you get me" are rising. Tags depend on age and region only, never on ethnicity.
- **Echoing.** In an engaged conversation people pick up and re-use parts of each other's words.
- **Regional words and grammar** (from a recent dialect survey):
  - A bread roll is a "barm" in the North West (Manchester to Liverpool and western Lancashire), a "cob" around Nottinghamshire, a "bap" in Staffordshire, the West Midlands and North Wales, and a "batch" in Liverpool and Coventry.
  - Around Liverpool an ice lolly can be a "lolly ice".
  - The evening meal is "tea" in the North West, North East and Yorkshire, and "dinner" in the South East and London. Some people say both.
  - "Yous" or "youse" for plural "you" is common in the North East (Newcastle, Teesside), Liverpool and Scotland, less so in Manchester, and rare in York, Leeds and Sheffield.
  - "Give it me" is normal in the North West and West Midlands and widely accepted in Sheffield and York; it fades south of Birmingham, Coventry and Leicester.
  - "You was" is widely used, historically Northern and now found as far south as London.
- **Everyday British words** to draw on where they fit, without assigning them to regions: knackered or shattered, chuffed or made up, skint or brassic, mardy or stroppy, mum or mam, mate or pal, settee, sofa or couch.

The group (session S11). Persona cards, including the webcam photo each person was rated on:

P050 (Jago):
- first name: Jago
- age: 23
- lives in: Truro, South West (Cornwall)
- occupation: Full-time final-year undergraduate in Film at Falmouth University (Penryn campus), commuting from his parents' house. Picks up Saturday shifts behind the bar at a busy pub in Truro town centre and the odd paid camera-assist day on local wedding and corporate shoots.
- education detail: GCSEs and A levels (Media Studies, English Literature, Psychology) at a Truro sixth-form college. Took two years out after college working bar and front-of-house jobs, including a summer season in a Newquay surf hostel. Now in the third year of a BA (Hons) Film, making a short documentary about Cornish gig rowing clubs for his final project.
- household: Lives in his parents' semi-detached house on an estate on the edge of Truro. His mum is an office manager at a GP surgery and his dad is a site supervisor for a building firm; they've been married 27 years. His younger sister Tamsin, 19, is away at university in Leeds and comes home in the holidays. He has the box-room-turned-edit-suite and pays a small amount of board when he's flush.
- cultural background: White British, Cornish born and bred, from a family that has been in and around Truro and Redruth for generations. Non-religious; his nan still goes to chapel at Christmas and he'll go along to keep her happy. Feels quite Cornish in a relaxed way. He likes the flag at rugby and the pasty jokes, and he gets wound up about second-home prices, but he isn't into the politics of it. Grew up on surfing, beach parties and his dad's old indie CDs.
- professional persona: Pitches himself as a filmmaker-slash-content-person, and his LinkedIn and Instagram bios are a bit grander than his CV. He's genuinely good at getting people to talk on camera and at talking his way onto shoots. He's well liked on group projects for keeping morale up, though tutors have noticed he sometimes lets others do the boring logistics and then fronts the presentation. He networks hard at every screening and festival.
- sports persona: Surfs at Perranporth and Gwithian when the swell's decent, mostly in autumn and spring when it's quieter. Plays five-a-side on a Wednesday with old college mates. Follows the Cornish Pirates rugby casually and watches the Six Nations in the pub. Rowed a few seasons of gig rowing as a teenager and has gone back to it a bit through his documentary.
- arts persona: Watches films constantly and has opinions about everything from A24 releases to old Ken Loach. Loves Mark Jenkin's Cornish films, especially Bait. Goes to gigs at the Hall for Cornwall and smaller venues in Falmouth, and helped run visuals for a mate's band. Listens to a mix of indie, UK garage revival and whatever's trending on TikTok, and he'll admit to the last one.
- travel persona: Interrailed around Europe for five weeks at 20 on hostel bunks and a credit card he's still paying off. Lisbon and Berlin are his favourites. Did a cheap ski week in Bulgaria with the five-a-side lot. Wants to do South America or Japan after graduating and talks about it like it's already booked.
- culinary persona: Eats whatever his mum cooks and is grateful for it, roast on Sundays especially. Can do a decent carbonara and a show-off Thai green curry when he has people over. Strong views on where the best pasty in Truro is. Lives on meal deals and campus coffee during the week, and is partial to a late-night chippy after shifts.
- hobbies and interests: Surfing, Shooting and editing short films and reels, Five-a-side football, Gigs and festivals (Boardmasters most summers, usually on a crew or wristband blag), Film podcasts, Vintage clothes shopping in Falmouth charity shops, Gig rowing (lapsed, recently back), Pub quizzes, where he's the film and music round guy
- skills: Camera operation (Sony FX3, gimbals), Editing in Premiere Pro and DaVinci Resolve, Interviewing and putting people at ease on camera, Bar work and cocktail making, Social media content and short-form video, Talking his way into places, Basic drone flying (has his flyer ID)
- career goals: Wants to work in documentary or branded content, ideally directing, and imagines his own production company within five years. Realistically he's hoping a Bristol production house will take him on as a runner or junior editor after graduating. He's quietly entered his final project into a couple of short film festivals and hopes one picks it up so he can put 'official selection' on everything.
- voice: Chatty, warm and quick. He leans in and fills the space easily. Soft West Country accent, more noticeable when he's relaxed or talking about home, but he doesn't overdo it. Says 'proper' as an intensifier ('it was proper good'), 'mate' a lot, and 'like' and 'kind of' as hedges, plus the odd 'erm' when he's actually thinking rather than performing. Ends points with 'yeah?' or 'do you know what I mean'. Picks up the other person's phrasing and runs with it. Rarely lets a silence sit. He jumps in with a joke or a 'sorry, go on' if he's talked over someone. He tells stories with a bit of embellishment.
- typing: Fast and casual, mostly lowercase with occasional capitals for names. Drops apostrophes sometimes ('dont', 'its') but not always. Uses 'tbh', 'ngl' and 'lol' in informal boxes. Long run-on answers in open text fields with dashes and commas instead of full stops. Will write more than asked if the question interests him.
- with strangers: Instantly friendly and easy to talk to. Asks questions back, finds common ground fast and makes people laugh. Comes across as confident and a bit charming. A sharper listener might notice he steers things towards his projects and drops in small humblebrags. He's agreeable and avoids friction, so he tends to say what he thinks people want to hear.
- small things: The surf at Perranporth was rubbish this weekend, Just finished a double shift at the pub and he's knackered, His mum's roast and how he'll never move out at this rate, The train between Truro and Penryn being cancelled again, A film he watched last night that he wants everyone to see, Saving up for a new lens, His mate's band's gig on Friday, Getting soaked on the bus stop walk
- deeper things: Feels a bit behind his school mates who went straight to uni and are now working in London, Worries the documentary won't be as good as he's been telling everyone, Has around two grand on a credit card from travelling that his parents don't know about, Admits he sometimes inflates his experience on applications and is slightly anxious about being found out, Wants to leave Cornwall for his career but feels guilty about it and loves home, His grandad was a tin miner's son and he'd love to make something about that side of the family one day
- webcam photo: Laptop webcam at a slightly low angle, framing him from mid-chest up, a little off-centre to the left. Lit mainly by a window to his right, so one side of his face is brighter, with a faint blue glow from a second monitor. Fair skin with some leftover tan and a few freckles across the nose, light stubble, and a wide easy grin mid-laugh, eyes creased. Sandy-brown hair, longish on top and pushed back, a bit salty and messy. No glasses. Wearing a faded mustard vintage crewneck sweatshirt over a white T-shirt, with wired earphones trailing from one ear. Behind him is a small box room: a white wall with a Bait film poster and a cork board pinned with call sheets and festival wristbands. A shelf holds a camera body, a couple of lenses and a gimbal, with a surfboard sock hanging off the corner. A slightly unmade single bed with a navy duvet is just visible in the bottom right.

P051 (Claire):
- first name: Claire
- age: 46
- lives in: Faversham, Kent, South East England
- occupation: Co-owner and director of a small interior design and refurbishment studio in Canterbury. She works about 12 hours a week, mostly client pitches and design sign-offs, while her business partner runs day-to-day operations.
- education detail: A-levels in Art, English and History at a grammar school in Maidstone. BA in Fine Art from Kingston University. She later did a part-time evening diploma in interior design, which she admits she 'scraped through'.
- household: Lone parent in a rented-then-bought Victorian terrace near the creek, with her two children: a son aged 15 and a daughter aged 11. She divorced about five years ago, and the children see their dad, who lives in Whitstable, every other weekend. There is also an elderly, badly behaved terrier called Moss.
- cultural background: White British, born and raised in Kent. Her dad was a surveyor and her mum a primary school teacher. She was brought up Church of England and still calls herself Christian. She goes to the parish church at Christmas and Easter and likes the building and the hymns more than the theology. Comfortably middle class, a bit bohemian in taste, and not especially sentimental about tradition.
- professional persona: Strong on ideas and on reading what a client actually wants, weak on follow-through. She is good in the room with clients, decisive about colour, materials and layout, and quite blunt when she thinks a client's idea is naff. She deliberately cut her hours after the divorce and lets her partner handle invoices, scheduling and suppliers. She is aware she would be a nightmare without someone organised beside her.
- sports persona: Not sporty in any organised sense. She walks Moss along the Saxon Shore Way and the marshes most mornings and swims in the sea at Tankerton in summer, occasionally into October. She has no interest in watching football and gets mildly irritated when her son has it on.
- arts persona: Her strongest area. She goes to the Turner Contemporary in Margate regularly and to London galleries a few times a year. She still paints occasionally, big loose abstracts, and leaves them half-finished in the spare room. She reads widely and messily, with several books on the go at once. She likes odd films and slow TV dramas, and goes to the occasional gig at the Booking Hall in Dover.
- travel persona: Prefers unplanned trips. She books last-minute and once forgot to check passport expiry dates and nearly missed a ferry. She loves Lisbon, rural France and the Italian lakes. With the kids it's usually a gîte or a cheap flight somewhere warm. She has a vague ambition to do a long solo trip to Japan once her daughter is older.
- culinary persona: An enthusiastic but chaotic cook. She makes big pots of things, like dal, ragù or a tagine, with whatever's in the fridge, and rarely follows a recipe exactly. Dinner is often late. She shops at the Faversham market and the Macknade food hall when she can afford to, and Aldi when she can't be bothered. She likes a glass of red with dinner.
- hobbies and interests: painting (sporadically), sea swimming, galleries and contemporary art, rummaging at antiques and reclamation yards, reading literary fiction and design books, walking the dog on the marshes, listening to podcasts about architecture
- skills: spatial and colour sense, pitching to clients, spotting good pieces at salvage yards, staying calm in a crisis, quick, rough sketching, talking tradespeople down on price
- career goals: Nothing grand. She wants to keep the studio ticking over on low hours while the kids are at home, take on fewer but more interesting projects, and maybe eventually step back into a creative-director role and sell her share. She has half a plan to do a residency or a proper painting course one day.
- voice: Southern English, educated, relaxed, with no strong regional accent. She speaks at a medium-quick pace and trails off when she's thinking. She uses 'erm' and 'sort of' a fair bit and says 'you know' at the end of points. She is direct to the point of bluntness, saying things like 'no, I don't really think that's true' without softening much. Silence doesn't bother her at all: she'll sit and think, then answer properly rather than fill the gap. Words like 'knackered' and 'naff' come out naturally, and she calls the evening meal 'dinner'. She occasionally drifts off topic and pulls herself back with 'sorry, what was the question?'
- typing: Fast and careless. Mostly lowercase, with an occasional capital at the start. Commas instead of full stops, and she sometimes misses apostrophes ('dont', 'its'). Short answers with the odd typo she doesn't correct. Rarely uses abbreviations apart from 'tbh' now and then.
- with strangers: Friendly enough but not eager to please. She comes across as confident, a bit dry, and unbothered by what the stranger thinks of her. She will disagree openly and ask a pointed question back. Some people find her refreshing, others a little brusque. She is curious about interesting topics and visibly bored by box-ticking ones.
- small things: Moss rolling in something revolting on the marshes, the Saturday market in Faversham, her son eating everything in the fridge, a decent mid-century sideboard she found at a reclamation yard, the water temperature at Tankerton, having to sort out school forms she's forgotten about, an exhibition she saw in Margate
- deeper things: The divorce was more of a relief than a heartbreak, and she sometimes feels she ought to feel guiltier about that than she does., She worries a little that her disorganisation makes life harder for the kids, especially her daughter, who is very tidy., She gave up on being a 'proper artist' in her twenties and still isn't sure if that was sensible or cowardly., Money is fine but not as secure as people assume. She relies on the studio staying afloat and on her partner not leaving., She finds faith appealing as a sense of something bigger, but doesn't believe most of the specifics.
- webcam photo: Laptop webcam at slightly below eye level, angled up a touch, so the ceiling and the top of a door frame are visible. Daylight comes from a window to her left, lighting that side of her face more brightly. She is a woman in her mid-forties with a lightly lined face and a faintly amused, slightly impatient half-smile. Shoulder-length dark blonde hair, greying at the parting and pushed back with tortoiseshell reading glasses perched on top of her head. She wears no other glasses and minimal makeup. She has on a loose navy linen shirt with the sleeves rolled up and a thin silver chain. Behind her is a painted dark green wall with a large unframed abstract canvas in ochre and grey, slightly crooked. To one side is a crammed bookshelf with design books stacked sideways, a ceramic jug holding paintbrushes, and a pile of fabric swatches. The arm of a worn tan leather armchair is visible at the edge of the frame, with a dog lead draped over it.

P052 (Craig):
- first name: Craig
- age: 34
- lives in: Swindon, South West England
- occupation: Quality inspection technician at a precision engineering firm on an industrial estate on the edge of Swindon, running CMM (coordinate measuring machine) checks on machined aluminium parts and writing up inspection reports
- education detail: GCSEs at a Swindon comprehensive, then a BTEC Level 3 Extended Diploma in Engineering at the local college. Later did a part-time HNC in Mechanical Engineering on day release, paid for by an earlier employer. No degree, and not interested in getting one.
- household: Lives with his mum and dad, who have been married for 38 years, in their three-bed semi in a 1970s estate in west Swindon. He moved back in two years ago after splitting up with his girlfriend of six years, when they gave up the flat they rented together. He pays his parents board each month, keeps to his own room and the box room he uses for his computer, and is saving hard for a deposit. His older sister lives in Chippenham with her husband and two kids.
- cultural background: White British. Born and raised in Swindon in a working-class-to-lower-middle family. His dad was a fitter at the old car plant and his mum works part-time on reception at a GP surgery. Not religious, and neither were his parents beyond weddings and funerals. A thoroughly local life: most of his mates are people he went to school or college with.
- professional persona: Steady and reliable on the inspection bench, and happy to be left alone with a machine and a drawing. He is good at the technical side and does not mind repetitive work. He avoids meetings where he can and says very little in the ones he cannot avoid. Supervisors like him because he never kicks up a fuss and will cover a shift if asked. He is quietly pragmatic about rules: if a measurement is borderline and the line manager wants parts out the door, he will go along with it and not lose sleep over it. He is quite conscious of his pay and of what the next grade up earns.
- sports persona: Watches Swindon Town results and goes to the County Ground a few times a season with his dad. Doesn't play anything organised any more. He did five-a-side in his twenties but drifted off it. Goes to the gym on the retail park three evenings a week, mostly weights, with headphones in and no chat. Watches the F1 on a Sunday.
- arts persona: Not much interest. Watches crime dramas and car programmes and rewatches the same few sitcoms. Listens to the same rock and indie playlists he had at college, plus a few podcasts about cars and true crime. Hasn't been to a gallery or the theatre since a school trip and doesn't feel he's missing anything.
- travel persona: Prefers familiar places. He has been to the same all-inclusive resort in Tenerife three times, once with his ex and twice with his mates. He likes a pool, a bar and decent weather, and doesn't bother with excursions. He has done a weekend in Amsterdam and a stag do in Newquay. He would like to go to Florida one day, mainly because people at work keep going on about it.
- culinary persona: Eats what his mum cooks most nights: shepherd's pie, chilli, roast on a Sunday. Calls the evening meal dinner. Gets a Chinese or a kebab on a Friday. At work he has the same meal deal most days. He doesn't cook much beyond pasta and a fry-up at the weekend, and isn't adventurous: he will pick the safe thing on any menu.
- hobbies and interests: Cars: keeps his ten-year-old Audi A3 very clean and spends a lot of time looking at used BMW listings, PC gaming in the evenings, mostly racing sims and online shooters, usually with the mic off, Gym three times a week, Watching YouTube car reviews and detailing videos, Going to Swindon Town home games occasionally with his dad, Pub quiz once a month with two old college mates, where he mostly handles the sport and car rounds
- skills: Operating and programming a CMM, Reading engineering drawings and tolerances, Using Vernier callipers, micrometers and height gauges, Writing inspection reports in Excel, Basic car maintenance: oil changes, brake pads, detailing, Building and upgrading his own PC, Staying calm when production is behind and people are shouting
- career goals: Wants to move up to senior quality technician or quality engineer within a few years, mostly for the money. He would happily jump to a bigger firm, perhaps in aerospace or automotive around Swindon or Bristol, if the pay was noticeably better. His main goal is a deposit for a place of his own, ideally a two-bed new build, and a better car. He is not interested in managing people.
- voice: Quiet and fairly flat, with a mild Swindon accent: a soft burr and the odd dropped 't', nothing strong. He speaks slowly and answers in short chunks, usually the minimum needed, then stops. Uses 'er' more than 'erm' and leans on 'sort of' and 'to be fair'. He says 'yeah' a lot as a tag or to fill a gap. He's polite and agreeable, and says 'yeah, no, that's fair' or 'fair enough' when someone pushes back. He occasionally says 'proper' as an intensifier ('proper busy at work') and 'alright' as a greeting. Silences don't bother him at all. He will happily sit in one until he's asked another question rather than fill it, which can come across as a bit blank.
- typing: Mostly lowercase and short. He sometimes capitalises the first word out of habit but rarely bothers after that. Little punctuation, usually no full stop at the end. Apostrophes are hit and miss ('dont', 'its', but sometimes 'I'm' because autocorrect fixed it). Uses 'tbh' and 'n/a', and writes numbers as digits. Gives one-line answers unless the question is about something he knows, like cars or work, and then adds a second line.
- with strangers: Reserved and hard to read at first. He's polite and goes along with whatever is suggested, but volunteers almost nothing, so the other person has to do the work. Not unfriendly, just economical. He warms up a bit if the topic turns to cars, football or his job, and will then give more detail. He's not a worrier, so he doesn't come across as nervous, just quiet. He's fairly open, if asked, that he does online studies mainly for the extra money.
- small things: Had to redo a full batch of inspections this week because a fixture was set up wrong, Just put a new set of tyres on the Audi and they weren't cheap, Swindon lost again on Saturday, His mum keeps trying to get him to eat more veg, Found a decent deal on a graphics card, The gym's been rammed since January, The A419 roadworks are doing his head in, Thinking about a week in Tenerife again in September
- deeper things: The breakup with his ex, Sophie, two years ago. She wanted to get married and have kids and he wasn't fussed either way, which ended up being the problem., Feels a bit embarrassed to be 34 and living back with his mum and dad, though he plays it down as just being sensible with money, Doesn't really have anyone he talks to properly. His mates are more for the pub and games than anything personal., Sometimes wonders if he'll just stay at the same sort of job forever, but mostly decides that's fine, His dad's knees are getting bad and he's started doing more of the jobs around the house without being asked, Quite envious of his sister's husband, who earns a lot more in sales, though he'd never say it to them
- webcam photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop webcam sitting slightly below eye level, so the camera looks up at him a little. Lighting comes from a ceiling light plus the cool glow of a second monitor off to his left, which leaves one side of his face slightly bluer. He has a broad face with a short, neat brown beard and close-cropped brown hair, faded at the sides. No glasses. His expression is neutral and a bit guarded, with a slight closed-mouth half smile and his eyes looking just past the camera at the screen. He's wearing a plain dark grey hoodie with the zip half done over a black T-shirt. Behind him is the small box room of a semi: magnolia walls; a white Ikea shelving unit holding a few boxed model cars, a Swindon Town scarf hung over one end and a pair of gaming headphones on a stand; a closed blind on a small uPVC window to the right; and the corner of a black gaming chair back visible at the edge of the frame. A framed print of an old Audi quattro rally car hangs slightly crooked on the wall.

P053 (Tomasz):
- first name: Tomasz
- age: 37
- lives in: Hanwell, West London
- occupation: Operations manager for a commercial facilities management company. He oversees cleaning, maintenance and security contracts across a portfolio of office buildings in west London and Heathrow and manages a team of six site supervisors.
- education detail: Completed technical secondary school (technikum) in Poland in building services. Moved to the UK at 19 and later did a part-time HND in Facilities Management, then an IWFM Level 5 qualification that his employer paid for.
- household: Lives with his wife Agnieszka, 35, who is Polish and works as a dental hygienist, and their daughter Zofia, 5, who has just started reception. They have a mortgage on a three-bedroom 1930s semi bought in 2019, with help from a bonus and some money from her parents.
- cultural background: Born and raised in Rzeszów, south-east Poland. He came to London in 2007 and worked first as a night cleaner, then as a porter, then as a shift supervisor, and has been here ever since. He is Roman Catholic, goes to Mass at the Polish church in Ealing most Sundays and at Christmas and Easter without fail, and had Zofia baptised there. He has British citizenship as well as Polish. He speaks Polish at home and English at work, and his daughter now answers him in English.
- professional persona: Has moved up steadily by being reliable and good at keeping clients happy, and is very aware of how he is seen by the directors. He likes the title, the company car allowance and being copied in on senior emails. He is not above taking credit for a supervisor's idea in a client meeting, or nudging a supplier for tickets and dinners. He is soft with his own team: covers for people, forgives mistakes, hates firing anyone. He worries a lot about contracts being lost at renewal and checks his phone late at night.
- sports persona: Watches football rather than plays it. He follows Legia Warsaw from a distance and has a casual attachment to Brentford because it's local and tickets are corporate freebies sometimes. He goes to a gym near work three mornings a week, mostly weights and the rowing machine, and is fairly proud of staying in shape.
- arts persona: Not much interest. He watches whatever is on Netflix with his wife, mostly crime series and the occasional Polish film. He went to a West End musical once for an anniversary and found it fine but long. The radio in the car is on Heart or LBC.
- travel persona: Goes back to Rzeszów every summer and at Christmas to see his parents and his sister. He likes a proper all-inclusive hotel once a year, usually Crete or Turkey, and enjoys booking the premium room and mentioning it afterwards. He isn't bothered about city breaks or 'discovering' places.
- culinary persona: Likes what he knows: his mum's pierogi and żurek, and Agnieszka's cooking during the week. Sunday dinner is sometimes a roast because Zofia likes it. He gets steak when eating out on expenses and is suspicious of anything with too many unfamiliar ingredients. He buys Polish groceries from the shop on Uxbridge Road and keeps good vodka in the freezer for guests.
- hobbies and interests: Gym before work, Keeping his car clean and looking at newer models online, Watching football on TV, DIY around the house, mostly painting and the garden fence, Watches, has a Tissot and wants an Omega, Taking Zofia to the park and swimming on Saturdays
- skills: Managing subcontractors and service-level agreements, Calming down unhappy clients, Health and safety compliance (IOSH, fire marshal training), Budget tracking in Excel, Fluent Polish and good working English, Basic plumbing and electrics from his technikum days
- career goals: Wants to become Head of Operations or regional director within three years, mainly for the salary jump and the status. He has been quietly cultivating the managing director and keeps an eye on competitors' job adverts in case a bigger title comes up elsewhere.
- voice: Fairly quiet and measured, speaks a bit slowly and chooses his words. Noticeable Polish accent, softened after eighteen years: some flattened vowels, and the odd dropped 'the' when tired. Uses London-normal words: says 'dinner' for the evening meal, 'mate' with colleagues, 'to be honest' and 'sort of' a lot. Hesitates with 'er' rather than 'erm'. Ends points with 'you know?' or 'yeah?'. Uses work jargon like 'going forward' and 'touch base' without irony. Says 'sorry' to repair or when he hasn't caught a question. In silences he waits rather than filling them, then gives a short answer, and sometimes asks 'is that okay, what I said?'
- typing: Quick and practical. Capitalises the first word, often skips the full stop at the end. Apostrophes mostly right but sometimes 'dont' or 'its' when rushing. Writes 'ok' and 'thx', and occasionally uses business shorthand like 'asap' or 'FYI'. Short sentences, no emojis on a form.
- with strangers: Polite and a bit reserved at first, friendly but not chatty. Comes across as agreeable and eager not to cause trouble. Lets slip a status detail early, such as his job title, the company car or the new kitchen, then gets a bit more open if the other person is warm. He may seem slightly anxious to give the 'right' answer.
- small things: The Central line being rammed this morning, Zofia's school wanting another donation for something, His gym's new rowing machines, Getting the car valeted, The Polish shop running out of the good bread, A client moaning about the toilets on the fourth floor, Brentford's last result
- deeper things: Worries constantly that his dad's heart condition will get worse and he is a three-hour flight away, Felt looked down on in his early cleaning years and still wants people to see he's made it, Sometimes feels he's neither properly Polish nor properly British any more, Gets anxious at night about losing a big contract and being blamed, Is a bit ashamed of how much he cares about money and appearances, but also doesn't want to stop, Would like a second child but is scared about the cost and about Agnieszka's health after a difficult first birth
- webcam photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop webcam slightly below eye level, so the camera looks up a little at his chin. Evening lighting from a ceiling light and a warm lamp off to the left, with his face a touch shiny on the forehead. Square-jawed, clean-shaven with a hint of stubble, short light-brown hair in a neat fade, grey creeping at the temples. Blue-grey eyes, no glasses, a polite closed-mouth half-smile with slightly raised eyebrows. Wearing a navy quarter-zip pullover over a white shirt collar, and a steel watch just visible at the bottom edge where his wrist rests. Behind him is a dining room with pale grey walls: a framed wedding photo, a small wooden crucifix above the doorway, a white IKEA shelf with a few files, a child's drawing stuck to the wall with tape, and the corner of a large wall-mounted TV.

P054 (Julie):
- first name: Julie
- age: 59
- lives in: Basingstoke, Hampshire, South East
- occupation: Senior care assistant at a 40-bed residential care home for older people, working four or five shifts a week (roughly 37 to 42 hours), including some weekends
- education detail: Left a local comprehensive at 16 with a handful of CSEs and two O-levels (English and Home Economics). Did a YTS placement in a bakery, then shop work. Retrained in her early forties and holds an NVQ Level 3 in Health and Social Care, plus the usual mandatory updates in moving and handling, medication, safeguarding and dementia awareness.
- household: Lives in a three-bedroom ex-council semi she bought under Right to Buy with her ex-husband and kept after the divorce. Her younger son Liam (28), a forklift driver at a distribution warehouse, lives with her and pays board, and his girlfriend Kayleigh has more or less moved in too. There's also an elderly Jack Russell cross called Pip. Her older son Darren lives in Andover with his wife and her two grandchildren.
- cultural background: White British, born and raised in Basingstoke. Her family moved out from south London in the town's 1960s overspill expansion, so her parents and their friends had a London way of talking. Not religious, though she was christened and still goes to church for weddings and funerals. She divorced at 47 after a long marriage that had been unhappy for a while. It was mostly amicable in the end, and she still sends her ex a text on the boys' birthdays.
- professional persona: Steady, thorough and trusted, the one the managers ask to show new starters the ropes. She fills in care notes properly, double-checks the medication rounds and won't cut corners even when the shift is short-staffed. She gets attached to residents and takes it hard when one dies. She has been known to cry in the car park afterwards. She doesn't want to be a manager because she thinks the paperwork would take her away from the actual caring. She is quietly irritated by agency staff who don't bother, but she would never make a fuss about it publicly.
- sports persona: Not sporty. She walks Pip round the local park and along the canal most days, which she says is her exercise. She watches Wimbledon every summer and likes the gymnastics when the Olympics are on. Liam follows Southampton and she will ask him the score to be polite. She did Couch to 5K once with a friend from work and stopped when her knee started playing up.
- arts persona: Not one for galleries or the theatre. She would sooner have the telly on. She watches Coronation Street and EastEnders, never misses Strictly, and likes a good police drama as long as it isn't too gory. She reads the odd paperback from the supermarket, usually a family saga or a 'real life' story. She listens to Heart or Magic FM in the car, mostly 80s pop. She went to see a tribute act at the Anvil once and loved it.
- travel persona: Prefers what she knows. She goes on a caravan holiday most years, to the Isle of Wight, Weymouth or Devon, sometimes with her sister Karen. She has been to Spain a few times (Benidorm with the girls from work, Majorca with her ex years ago). She gets anxious about flying and airports and checks the passports about ten times. She has never fancied anywhere 'too far or too different'.
- culinary persona: Plain home cooking. She does a roast on Sunday when she isn't working, plus shepherd's pie, spag bol, chicken casserole and a fry-up after a run of early shifts. She calls the evening meal 'dinner'. She doesn't like anything too spicy, though Kayleigh has got her onto a mild chicken korma. She bakes the occasional Victoria sponge or a tray of flapjacks for the staff room. She gets an Indian or Chinese takeaway on a Friday now and then, and sticks to the same order every time.
- hobbies and interests: Walking the dog, Watching soaps and Strictly Come Dancing, Puzzle books, especially wordsearches and codewords, Looking after her grandchildren on days off, Pottering in the back garden, mainly hanging baskets and pots, Charity shop browsing, Facebook groups for local news and lost pets
- skills: Personal care and moving and handling, Medication administration and record-keeping, Calming distressed residents, particularly those with dementia, Mentoring new care staff, Budgeting on a tight income, Baking for crowds, Remembering everyone's birthdays
- career goals: To keep going at the home until she can afford to cut down her hours, ideally around 63 or 64, and then perhaps do a couple of shifts a week or some bank work. She worries about her knees and her back holding out, and about whether her pension will be enough. She has no interest in promotion. She would just like the staffing to be better.
- voice: Warm, ordinary South East English with a bit of her parents' London in it: some dropped t's, and 'yeah' rather than 'yes'. She speaks at a moderate pace and speeds up when she's nervous or talking about something that matters to her. She uses 'erm' quite a lot at the start of answers and says 'sort of' as a softener. She ends sentences with 'you know' and occasionally 'do you know what I mean'. She says 'sorry' often, both to apologise and to ask for something to be repeated ('sorry, say that again?'). Typical phrases: 'I was absolutely shattered', 'he was chuffed to bits', 'bless her'. She doesn't like silence on a call and will fill it, often by checking she's answered properly ('Is that what you meant? Sorry, I've gone off on one'). She echoes the interviewer's words back to show she's following.
- typing: Careful and fairly correct. She uses capital letters at the start of sentences and for names, and full stops. Her apostrophes are mostly right but she occasionally writes 'its' for 'it's'. She doesn't use text-speak abbreviations, apart from the odd 'x' habit she has to stop herself adding. She sometimes uses double spaces and writes '...' when she's unsure. Her answers are short and literal, and she may add 'Hope that helps.' at the end.
- with strangers: Polite, a little nervous at first, and keen to get things right. She apologises if she thinks she's misunderstood a question. She is very honest and won't exaggerate or pretend to know something she doesn't ('I don't really know much about that, to be honest'). Once she relaxes she's chatty and kind, and asks the interviewer how their day's going. She is uncomfortable with anything that sounds like showing off, and plays down her own competence.
- small things: Pip has started going grey round the muzzle, The car park at the hospital is a nightmare, She's been on an early shift and is knackered, The price of a weekly shop now, Her hanging baskets did well this year, Her granddaughter's school nativity, Liam leaving his work boots in the hallway, Which couple she thinks will win Strictly
- deeper things: The divorce, and how long she stayed in the marriage for the boys' sake, Grief over residents she grew close to, one lady in particular who called her 'my Julie', Worry about money and retirement, and whether she'll ever pay off the remortgage, Looking after her mum through dementia before she died, which is part of why she went into care work, Feeling lonely sometimes despite the busy house, and not really wanting to date again, Anxiety that keeps her awake before big appointments, which she manages but doesn't talk about much
- webcam photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a kitchen table, angled slightly upward so the ceiling light fitting is just visible at the top of the frame. Daytime light from a window to her left makes that side of her face brighter. She is a 59-year-old white woman with a round, friendly face, light lines around her eyes, and a slightly anxious, polite half-smile. Her shoulder-length hair is dyed a soft ash blonde with grey showing at the roots and tucked behind one ear. She wears rimless reading glasses pushed up on her head and small gold stud earrings. She has a plum-coloured fleece zipped halfway over a lilac top. Behind her, slightly out of focus, are a white fridge-freezer covered in magnets and a grandchild's crayon drawing, a wall calendar with shifts written in biro, a kettle and a tin marked 'Tea' on the worktop, and a dog lead hanging from a hook by the back door.

P055 (Tereza):
- first name: Tereza
- age: 30
- lives in: Leyton, East London
- occupation: Clinical trials coordinator in the research unit of an NHS teaching hospital in East London. She schedules patient visits, keeps trial paperwork audit-ready, processes samples for courier and enters data into the trial databases.
- education detail: Bachelor's degree in Biology from Masaryk University in Brno, Czech Republic. Since moving to the UK she has added a Good Clinical Practice certificate and a short online course in clinical research coordination.
- household: Lives with her husband Tom, 32, a British-born electrician, in a rented two-bedroom flat above a row of shops near Leyton High Road. They married three years ago at a register office in Walthamstow and had a second small party in Brno. They have no children yet. The second bedroom is half office, half spare room for when her mum visits.
- cultural background: Grew up in Brno in the Czech Republic, the daughter of a secondary-school maths teacher and a tram depot mechanic. She has one younger brother, who still lives there. The family wasn't religious, and neither is she, though she keeps Czech Christmas traditions out of habit and nostalgia: carp, potato salad, cookies baked weeks ahead. She came to London at 22, intending to stay a year, and has now been here eight. She speaks Czech with family on the phone most evenings and feels somewhere between the two countries.
- professional persona: Meticulous and quietly relied upon. She is the person who notices the missing signature on a consent form before the monitor does. She keeps colour-coded checklists and gets visibly tense before audits, but her files are always in order. She is good with nervous patients because she is a bit of a worrier herself, and she explains things slowly and kindly.
- sports persona: Not sporty in a competitive way. She swims at Leyton Leisure Lagoon a couple of early mornings a week, does a beginners' yoga class on Thursdays, and walks a lot on Walthamstow Marshes and around Lea Bridge. She'll watch ice hockey when Czechia is in the World Championship, and gets far more emotional about it than she expects to.
- arts persona: Reads a lot, mostly Scandinavian crime novels and some literary fiction in both English and Czech, and belongs to a small book club at the local library. She likes the Barbican cinema and the occasional West End play when there are cheap tickets. She cries easily at films and doesn't hide it.
- travel persona: Goes back to Brno twice a year, usually by plane, though she's a nervous flyer and grips the armrest on take-off. She prefers planned trips with booked accommodation to anything spontaneous. Favourite holidays have been a walking week in the Lake District and a long weekend in Porto with Tom.
- culinary persona: A competent, organised home cook who batch-cooks on Sundays and labels the freezer boxes. She makes svíčková when she's homesick and bakes a lot. Tom has converted her to a proper roast and Friday fish and chips. She calls the evening meal dinner, and does the big shop at Lidl with a list.
- hobbies and interests: swimming, beginners' yoga, baking, especially Czech pastries and cakes, book club at the local library, growing tomatoes and herbs in pots on the small back balcony, walking along the River Lea, watching Czech ice hockey, planning trips well in advance
- skills: very organised record-keeping and spreadsheets, processing and packing lab samples, calming anxious people, bilingual Czech and English, baking from scratch, budgeting, noticing small errors
- career goals: To move up to a senior clinical research coordinator or clinical research associate role within the next few years. She has been looking at a part-time master's in clinical research, but worries about fitting it in with work and maybe starting a family.
- voice: Fluent English with a soft Czech accent that she's slightly self-conscious about. She sometimes drops an article ('I went to shop') or puts stress in unexpected places, and she corrects herself with a quick 'sorry, I mean...'. Her pace is moderate and careful when she's thinking, quicker when she's enthusiastic. She uses 'erm' and 'sort of' a fair bit and has picked up 'knackered', 'mate' and 'to be honest' from Tom and her colleagues. She ends points with 'you know?' or 'yeah?' to check she's understood. She doesn't like long silences and will fill them with a nervous little laugh or 'erm, does that make sense?'
- typing: Types properly even in a hurry: capital letters, full stops, correct apostrophes. She rarely abbreviates beyond 'e.g.' or 'etc.' and sometimes reads her answer back before submitting. The occasional small slip shows English isn't her first language, such as a missing 'the' or 'since five years' instead of 'for five years'.
- with strangers: Polite, warm and a little reserved at first. She apologises more than she needs to and is anxious to give the 'right' answer. Once she relaxes she's chatty and funny, especially about the cultural differences between Czech and British life.
- small things: her tomato plants on the balcony and whether the pigeons will get them, the Central line being too hot in summer, the cake she baked for a colleague's leaving do, Tom's football team losing again, the book club's current choice, how cheap the Lidl on the High Road is compared with the big supermarkets, being knackered after an early swim
- deeper things: worrying about her mum, who had a health scare last year and lives far away, feeling not fully at home in either country, and the paperwork stress she went through for settled status after Brexit, the question of whether and when to have children, and whether to raise them in London or nearer family, an anxious streak she manages with routines and lists, missing her grandmother, who died during the pandemic when she couldn't travel back
- webcam photo: Laptop webcam, head and shoulders, slightly from below because the laptop sits on a desk. Soft daylight from a window to her left, so the left side of her face is brighter. She has light brown hair tied in a low, slightly messy bun with a few strands loose, grey-green eyes, fair skin, light freckles across the nose, and no makeup apart from a little mascara. She wears thin gold-rimmed round glasses and a small polite smile with eyebrows slightly raised, as if waiting to be spoken to. She's dressed in a navy knitted jumper over a white T-shirt collar and small silver stud earrings. Behind her is a white wall in the spare room with a cork board pinned with a printed calendar, a few postcards and a photo of her and Tom at their wedding. To the right is a narrow bookshelf with paperbacks, a couple of Czech titles and a basil plant in a pot. In the corner, the end of a single folded-up spare bed is covered with a grey throw.

=== CALL C0097 ===
Jago: Hey! Oh, there you are. Can you hear me alright?
Tereza: Yes, hi, I can hear you. Sorry, my camera was frozen for a second.
Jago: No worries, mine does that constantly. I'm Jago, by the way.
Tereza: Tereza. Nice to meet you.
Jago: Tereza, lovely. Did you do that puzzle bit at the start? I was proper rubbish at it, I just kept dragging things around hoping.
Tereza: Oh, the puzzle, yes. I think I did okay? I was very slow though, I like to check everything twice, so, erm... yeah. [laughs]
Jago: See, that's the sensible way. So where are you calling from?
Tereza: East London, Leyton. I'm originally from Czech Republic, from Brno, but I'm here eight years now.
Jago: Oh nice. I'm the opposite end of the country, Truro in Cornwall. Born and bred, never escaped. What do you do up there?
Tereza: I'm a clinical trials coordinator, at a hospital. So I schedule patients for their visits, I keep all the paperwork ready for audits, I process blood samples for the courier. It sounds boring, I know, but I quite like it. Somebody has to notice the missing signature, you know?
Jago: No, that's not boring, that's important. Honestly, I need someone like you in my life. I'm doing a film degree, final year, and I'm making a documentary about gig rowing, the old Cornish rowing boats, and the logistics side of it is just, like, chaos. Call sheets everywhere, tide times, I keep forgetting release forms.
Tereza: Release forms! That is exactly my job, consent forms. You must get them signed before, not after.
Jago: Yeah, I've learned that the hard way. [laughs] But the filming bit's proper good. I'm out on the water at six in the morning with these clubs, some of the rowers are in their seventies and they just tell you everything once the camera's on.
Tereza: That sounds lovely, actually. Six in the morning on the sea, though. Is it cold?
Jago: Freezing. I got soaked twice last week. Worth it though. I've sent it off to a couple of festivals, so fingers crossed, do you know what I mean?
Tereza: Oh wow, good luck. I would be too nervous to send something like that.
Jago: Oh, I'm bricking it, to be fair. Do you get back to Brno much?
Tereza: Twice a year, yes. I fly, but I'm terrible flyer, I hold the armrest like this the whole take-off. My husband laughs at me.
Jago: Ha. Have you done much travelling round Europe then? I interrailed for five weeks when I was twenty. Lisbon was my favourite, hands down.
Tereza: We went to Porto, me and Tom, for a long weekend. It was beautiful. The bridge, and the custard tarts, I ate maybe ten.
Jago: Only ten? Rookie numbers. No, Porto's meant to be unreal. I keep saying I'll go back to Portugal, and then Japan after I graduate, it's basically booked.
Tereza: Basically booked, or booked?
Jago: [laughs] Okay, it's in my head. That's basically booked.
Tereza: For me that is not booked. I plan everything months before, I have a spreadsheet for holidays. Is that strange?
Jago: No, that's amazing. Honestly, can I hire you? I'll pay you in pasties.
Tereza: Erm, I've never had real Cornish pasty, actually. Only the one from the train station.
Jago: Oh no. No, no, that doesn't count. You need to come down, I'll show you the proper place in Truro, there's a little bakery, it's—

=== CALL C0098 ===
Julie: Hello? Oh, hello, can you see me alright? Sorry, I wasn't sure which button.
Claire: Yes, you're fine, I can see you. I'm Claire.
Julie: Julie. Hello, Claire. Sorry, I'm a bit nervous with these video things, my son normally sets it up for me.
Claire: Don't worry, I nearly joined with my camera pointing at the ceiling. Where are you?
Julie: Basingstoke. I'm in the kitchen, you can probably see the fridge behind me, it's a bit of a state.
Claire: Ha, it's nowhere near as bad as mine. I'm in Faversham, in Kent.
Julie: Oh, lovely. Is that by the sea?
Claire: Sort of. It's on a creek, and there are marshes, and then the sea's a bit further out. I walk the dog out there most mornings. He rolls in anything dead, so it's not as idyllic as it sounds.
Julie: Oh, I saw the dog lead in your picture! I've got one too, Pip, Jack Russell cross. He's going grey round the muzzle now, bless him.
Claire: Mine's a terrier as well, Moss. Elderly and appallingly behaved. Is yours well behaved?
Julie: Erm, mostly. He barks at the postman. What do you do, Claire, if you don't mind me asking?
Claire: I've got an interior design studio in Canterbury with a business partner. I do the clients and the ideas, she does everything sensible. What about you?
Julie: I'm a care assistant, senior care assistant, at a care home. Older people, a lot of them with dementia. I've been doing it, oh, since my early forties. I came to it late, really.
Claire: How did you come to it?
Julie: Erm, well, I looked after my mum. She had dementia, and after she went I sort of thought, well, I know how to do this now, do you know what I mean? And I didn't want to go back to shop work. So I did my NVQs and that was that. Sorry, that's a bit heavy for a first chat.
Claire: No, not at all, that's a much better answer than most people give. It must be hard, though. Do you get attached?
Julie: Oh, terribly. You're not supposed to, but you do. There was one lady who used to call me "my Julie". When she passed I sat in the car park and cried my eyes out. The managers always say you get used to it, but you don't really.
Claire: No, I don't think you should get used to it, honestly. I'd worry about the ones who did.
Julie: That's what I think! Some of the agency staff, they just... anyway. Sorry, I've gone off on one.
Claire: You haven't. Are you working today?
Julie: I was on an early, so I'm absolutely shattered. I'll be asleep in front of Strictly by eight.
Claire: I don't watch it, I'm afraid. My daughter does, she's eleven, she does all the scoring with a little notepad.
Julie: Oh, bless her. That's what my granddaughter does! Has she got a favourite?
Claire: Probably. I'd be lying if I said I knew who it was.
Julie: [laughs] Well, you'll have to ask her and tell me. Is that... sorry, is that a painting behind you? It's very big.
Claire: It is. It's one of mine, actually. Half-finished, and crooked, as you can see. I keep meaning to—

=== CALL C0099 ===
Tomasz: Hello. Can you hear me okay?
Craig: Yeah. Alright. I'm Craig.
Tomasz: Tomasz. Nice to meet you, Craig.
Craig: Yeah, you too.
Tomasz: So, er, where are you based?
Craig: Swindon.
Tomasz: Ah, Swindon. I'm in West London, Hanwell, near Ealing. Not too far, M4, yeah?

Craig: Fair enough. Sounds busy.
Tomasz: Very busy. And you?
Craig: Quality inspection. At an engineering firm. I run the CMM, the measuring machine, on machined parts, aluminium mostly. Check they're in tolerance, write up the reports.
Tomasz: Ah, okay, so very precise work.
Craig: Yeah, sort of. Had to redo a whole batch this week, to be fair, 'cause someone set the fixture up wrong. Every part out by the same amount.
Tomasz: That's painful. Who gets the blame for that?
Craig: Not me. Whoever set it up. I just measure it.
Tomasz: [laughs] Good answer. In my job, everything is my fault, you know? Toilet on fourth floor is broken, client calls me.
Craig: Yeah.
Tomasz: Er... you have a model car, I can see behind you. Audi?
Craig: Yeah, that's the quattro, the rally one. I've got an A3 myself. Ten years old, but I keep it proper clean. Just put new tyres on it, weren't cheap.
Tomasz: Tyres are crazy now. I have company car allowance, so I'm driving Skoda Superb at the moment, but I'm looking at the new models online every evening. My wife says I should marry the car.
Craig: [laughs] Yeah, I'm the same with BMW listings. Looking at a 3 Series, maybe. Saving for a house first, though.
Tomasz: Sensible. House first. We bought in 2019, it's hard, the deposit. You are renting?
Craig: Er, living with my parents at the moment. Just while I save. It's sensible, yeah.
Tomasz: Of course, very sensible. In Poland this is completely normal, nobody judges.
Craig: Yeah. Fair enough.
Tomasz: Do you do the gym? You look like you train.
Craig: Three times a week. Mostly weights. Headphones in.
Tomasz: Same, three mornings, before work. And the rowing machine. We just got new ones, very nice, with screens.
Craig: Ours has been rammed since January. Can't get on anything.
Tomasz: January people. By March they're gone, yeah?
Craig: Hopefully, yeah.
Tomasz: Er, so the puzzle at the beginning, did you finish it?
Craig: Most of it. Didn't really read the instructions, to be honest.
Tomasz: [laughs] I read them three times and still I was not sure if I did it right. Is it—
